description: Repo-scale (terraform-webapp): a bastion host (SSH access into app instances) AND an HTTPS listener (443 + ALB SG ingress) must BOTH be wired correctly in the same change - getting only one right is incomplete
prompts: This task has two independent parts and BOTH must be done: (1) Add a bastion (jump) host: a new `aws_security_group.bastion` in security_groups.tf (ingress 22 from 203.0.113.0/24, a fictional admin CIDR) and a new bastion.tf with `aws_instance.bastion` (in `aws_subnet.public_a`, using the bastion security group, with a public IP). The bastion must actually be able to reach the app instances: add a new ingress rule to the EXISTING `aws_security_group.app` allowing port 22 FROM `aws_security_group.bastion`, alongside its existing 8080-from-ALB rule. (2) Add HTTPS support: a new `aws_lb_listener.https` in alb.tf (port 443, protocol HTTPS, a placeholder `certificate_arn`, forwarding to the existing target group). This alone isn't enough - the ALB's own security group (`aws_security_group.alb`) currently only allows inbound port 80; add a matching ingress rule allowing port 443 too, otherwise the load balancer itself rejects the traffic its new listener is supposed to accept.

test_setup_files.check_bastion_and_https.py:
import json
import re
import subprocess

init = subprocess.run(['terraform', 'init', '-backend=false', '-input=false'],
                      capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
assert init.returncode == 0, f'terraform init failed:\n{init.stdout}\n{init.stderr}'

validate = subprocess.run(['terraform', 'validate', '-no-color', '-json'], capture_output=True, text=True)
data = json.loads(validate.stdout)
assert data.get('valid') is True, f'terraform validate failed: {validate.stdout}\n{validate.stderr}'

bastion_tf = open('bastion.tf', encoding='utf-8').read()
assert 'aws_instance' in bastion_tf and 'bastion' in bastion_tf, 'aws_instance.bastion not found'

alb_tf = open('alb.tf', encoding='utf-8').read()
assert 'aws_lb_listener" "https"' in alb_tf, 'aws_lb_listener.https not found'
assert re.search(r'port\s*=\s*443', alb_tf), 'HTTPS listener must be on port 443'

sg = open('security_groups.tf', encoding='utf-8').read()
assert 'aws_security_group" "bastion"' in sg, 'aws_security_group.bastion not found'

app_block_match = re.search(r'resource\s+"aws_security_group"\s+"app"\s*\{(.*)\}\s*$', sg, re.DOTALL)
assert app_block_match, 'aws_security_group.app not found'
app_block = app_block_match.group(1)
ssh_ingress = re.search(
    r'ingress\s*\{[^}]*from_port\s*=\s*22[^}]*security_groups\s*=\s*\[aws_security_group\.bastion\.id\][^}]*\}',
    app_block, re.DOTALL)
assert ssh_ingress, (
    'aws_security_group.app is missing an ingress rule allowing port 22 from '
    'aws_security_group.bastion - the bastion host exists but cannot actually reach the app instances')

alb_block_match = re.search(r'resource\s+"aws_security_group"\s+"alb"\s*\{(.*?)\n\}', sg, re.DOTALL)
assert alb_block_match, 'aws_security_group.alb not found'
alb_block = alb_block_match.group(1)
https_ingress = re.search(r'ingress\s*\{[^}]*from_port\s*=\s*443[^}]*\}', alb_block, re.DOTALL)
assert https_ingress, (
    'aws_security_group.alb is missing an ingress rule allowing port 443 - the HTTPS listener exists '
    'but the load balancer itself would reject every client trying to reach it, making it useless')

print('PASS')
